summary.prose: When a stage is reassigned in the tracker, the previous owner's next changing action is refused as today and now also offers to park: the draft artifacts and a checkpoint of the run (its complete state, who owned it and which upstream artifact revisions it started from) are committed to a handoff branch named from the repo's branch pattern, pushed, and noted on the stage's issue. The new assignee resumes with one command: the daemon checks the repository is registered and is the same one, fetches the branch, restores the files, rebinds the run to their clone and returns the next workflow turn, whichever stage the run was in. If there is no parked branch, for instance after a lost machine, resume tells them which stage to start afresh on the committed artifacts, so finished stages are never redone.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: A daemon-side team gate over a synchronous, capability-declaring tracker port (alternative a1). The port (sc1) is the only way the workflow library talks to a tracker; GitHub is its first adapter, made by extracting the existing GitHub code (src/workflow/tracker, the issue calls in tracker-auto.ts, and the create and close calls in src/workflow/bugfix/tracker.ts) behind it. sc1 is the one tracker abstraction: the unbuilt tracker-tool design (LLD-38436e90625a83a2-S001) is not built as a second abstraction and is superseded or amended by s1's LLD. The policy (sc2) is read from the remote default branch and says which stages need signoff, whether claims are enforced, the claim units and the administrators. The artifact's tracker record keeps every existing meta.tracker field exactly as it is and gains additive per-unit data, plus an optional meta.revision (sc3). The team gate (sc4) takes a guarded action and returns an outcome. Signoff is a separate record (sc5) that never changes meta.review or approvedAt. Syncing tracker status on git pull and push, and the issue-status read it needs, are deferred with the later-tracker work to a define extend and are not part of this HLD.

consumedContracts.name: Team gate, claim state, gate outcome, refusal error and completion hook
consumedContracts.purpose: The single gate for guarded actions in the daemon-owned workflow library, the claim state read live from the tracker, the outcome type, the typed refusal error that leaves approval, the review-fix decision that both review paths (verdicts.ts and run-artifact.ts) consult, and a completion hook that s5 ships unregistered and s7 registers. The gate derives the acting user itself through the port, so no caller signature changes. Owned by s5; s4 supplies issue creation which the gate calls for the no-issue outcome.

boundary.internal: Parking a draft on a handoff branch, the issue note, resuming from committed files, and reconstructing in-flight workflow state from committed artifacts instead of the opaque token.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The GitHub adapter built by extracting src/workflow/tracker (including the existing signed-in-user read, ghCurrentLogin, behind whoAmI), the issue calls in tracker-auto.ts and the create and close calls in src/workflow/bugfix/tracker.ts behind the port; the gh command wrapper with its 10-second timeout; contract tests; detection of a missing tool or sign-in. The port receives the needed capabilities as an argument, so s1 does not read the policy. Reconciliation: the unbuilt tracker-tool design LLD-38436e90625a83a2-S001 (docs/standalone/add-add-items-tracker-setting-have-E2026100638436e90/S001/LLD.md) is not built as a second abstraction; sc1 is the one tracker abstraction and s1's LLD supersedes or amends that LLD, once its conflicting approval status is settled. Syncing tracker status on git pull and push, and an issue-status read on the port, are deferred to the define extend.

Reading the policy file from the remote default branch ref, the cached last-fetched copy and the offline rule, finding the first default-branch commit that carried the policy file, the starter policy and the team setup command.

The repo-scoped kind of row in the shared settings catalog whose reads and writes go to the per-repo map in github.json read by resolveGithubConfig; its rendering in VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal client; read-only display of policy values. Shares the single store with s1's target resolution.

Shared issue-creation code refactored out of autoPushEpicOnHld, autoPushStoryOnLld and autoPushTasksOnPlan, find-by-label dedupe for Story and Task issues, forcing Task issues on in team mode, daemon-side triggering when a draft is first written, the terminal approve path kept as manual fallback, the inventory and classification of artifact write paths (including the two writeFileSync writers, and both verdicts.ts and run-artifact.ts as content writes when auto-fixes change the body), the single content-write helper and the revision minting, the bypass test that also detects raw writeFileSync on artifact paths, and the rule that an artifact without meta.revision reads as revision 0.

The team gate and its call sites (daemon step entry points and approveArtifactByJsonPath), the acting-user read through the port, claim and release commands, live assignee reads, the guarded-action list (code-review and analyze are never guarded; review is never refused), the report-only review for a non-holder through the review-fix decision on both review paths (verdicts.ts and run-artifact.ts), the typed TeamGateRefusedError, its handling beside ReviewBlockedError in approveWorkflowTarget and its formatting in the terminal client's approve case in src/cli/command.ts, the no-issue outcome handling, administrator release, and the declaration of the completion hook, shipped unregistered.

Opening the signoff request with the chosen artifacts, prerequisite checks for model review and local approval, registering the completion hook to produce the awaiting-signoff outcome, the on-demand completion check, automatic release of the claim on completion, recording sign-off together, grandfathering of artifacts approved before the policy anchor, and the separate display of signoff.
Revision of an open request: re-run of local approval, push to the same request, discarding an earlier completion, refusing non-holders.
Private implementation of s9: Keep tracker issues and status in step with the work without a manual step

nonFunctional.performance: Each guarded action makes at most two live reads through the port (the signed-in user and the assignee); every tracker command has a 10-second timeout, after which the action is refused with the reason. A repo without a policy makes no tracker call.
nonFunctional.security: Policy is read only from the remote default branch ref and is not locally overridable; enforcement lives in the daemon-owned workflow library (k1); no tracker secrets are stored by insrc, sign-in stays with the tracker's CLI; administrators come only from the policy.
nonFunctional.observability: Every gate outcome other than allowed is logged with unit, action and reason; port failures carry their kind (missing-tool, missing-signin, unreachable, rejected).
nonFunctional.durability: Claim, issue and signoff state live in the tracker and in committed artifact files; the in-memory step state stores (100 entries, 1 hour) are not relied on for handoff. Artifact writes stay atomic through the existing helper.

dataModelChanges.details: Written to .insrc/handoff/<unit-key>.json on the handoff branch only, as one of two variants. Common: schemaVersion (1), kind ('run' | 'draft'), unit (epicHash, storyId), parkedBy, parkedAt, sourceHead, repositoryId (the root commit id), artifactPaths (repo-relative files parked with it). RunCheckpoint adds: runId, epicKey, stage (awaiting_plan, awaiting_llm_step or awaiting_synthesize), intent (workflow, focus, params; repoPath and repoIndexedAt are not stored), executor (plan, nextStepIndex, stepOutputs, pause; its own intent is not stored) when stage is awaiting_llm_step, stepOutputs when awaiting_synthesize, owner, upstream (the { artifactId, revision } snapshot captured when the run was created). A DraftCheckpoint carries only the common fields: it is for a daemon that restarted or a draft with no live run. Restoring checks every path lies under the unit's own artifact paths.

Each entry gains optional meta { owner, upstream } beside payload, createdAt and touchedAt, and the module gains listStates. meta is set by handleStart through encodeState and carried by reencodeState and replaceState. Runs created when claims are not enforced, or before this change, have no meta.owner and are never treated as the actor's: they make offerPark false and park refuses them.

offerPark was always false. It is now true when the registered park-offer provider returns true for (repo, unit, actor): the actor owns a live run for the unit in any stage or has an uncommitted draft artifact for it. The type is unchanged.
A held-by-other outcome with offerPark true appends the park command, so every client that prints the refusal also prints the offer.
The catalog row gains the default insrc/handoff/{type}-{id} and loses its not-used-yet note; the grammar's placeholders stay id, slug and type.
One comment: the marker '<!-- insrc:handoff -->', the branch, the checkpoint commit, who parked, the stage and the variant. Posted with port.issueOps.comment; nothing reads it back.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Reads GateOutcome and TeamGateRefusedError unchanged. resumeStage asks teamGate with action 'author' and the workflow, which claims an unassigned unit through the add-only assignment. parkDraft reads the holder through the same gate read and refuses when the actor holds the unit. The only addition to sc4 is registerParkOfferProvider, proposed as an amendment so offerPark can be set without an import cycle.

errorCases.scenario: Park is requested while the actor holds the unit
errorCases.detection: parkDraft reads the holder through the gate and finds the actor's own login
errorCases.response: Return ok:false 'you hold this stage; there is nothing to hand over'. Nothing is written
errorCases.userImpact: A clear refusal instead of a branch for work the user still owns

errorCases.scenario: The unit is a Task, or has no issue, or has no holder
errorCases.detection: parkDraft checks unit.unit and the gate read: a Task unit, a no-issue outcome or a null holder
errorCases.response: Return ok:false naming the reason; a Task has no run to checkpoint and an unassigned unit is claimed and continued, not parked
errorCases.userImpact: The user is told to claim or to commit their code normally

errorCases.scenario: Nothing to park: the actor owns no run for the unit and has no uncommitted draft artifact
errorCases.detection: listStates has no entry whose meta.owner is the actor and whose intent maps to the unit, and git status --porcelain on the unit's artifact paths is empty
errorCases.response: Return ok:false 'no draft or run to hand over'

errorCases.scenario: A supplied run token belongs to another unit, another actor, or a run with no owner
errorCases.detection: The store entry's intent unit, meta.owner and the actor are compared before anything is read from git
errorCases.response: Return ok:false naming which comparison failed; nothing is written
errorCases.userImpact: A user cannot park someone else's run or a run from another stage

errorCases.scenario: Branch name breaks the grammar or does not identify the unit
errorCases.detection: handoffBranchName validates the filled name against the branchPattern row grammar and requires {id} in the pattern
errorCases.response: Return ok:false with the rule broken; no git command runs
errorCases.userImpact: The user fixes the pattern in settings

errorCases.scenario: Git fails while parking (not a repository, hook rejects the commit, push rejected, remote unreachable)
errorCases.detection: runGit returns ok:false for the failing step
errorCases.response: Stop at that step, remove the temporary worktree and the local branch this call created, leave the run in the store untouched, and report the git message with the step name. A rejected push because the branch moved reports that someone else parked first
errorCases.userImpact: Nothing is lost: the run stays in the daemon and the working files stay where they are

errorCases.scenario: The issue note cannot be posted
errorCases.response: Keep the pushed branch, return ok:true with noted:false and the failure kind, and print the branch name so the user can tell the new owner
errorCases.userImpact: Handoff works but the issue lacks the pointer until the user says it

errorCases.scenario: The receiving path is not registered with the daemon, or is a different repository from the checkpoint's
errorCases.detection: verifyReceivingRepo compares the path with listRepos and the checkpoint's repositoryId with git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD, before the branch is fetched into the working tree or any file is restored; resolveRepoPath alone would accept any non-empty path
errorCases.response: Return refused naming whether it is unregistered, not a git repository or another repository; nothing is restored and no state is saved
errorCases.userImpact: The new owner registers the repository, or opens the right clone

errorCases.scenario: Resume finds a checkpoint with an unknown schemaVersion, an unknown kind, a unit that does not match, or a path outside the unit's artifact paths
errorCases.detection: Parsing and validating the checkpoint before anything is written
errorCases.response: Return refused with the specific field; no file is restored and no state is saved
errorCases.userImpact: The new owner is told the checkpoint is unusable and may start the stage afresh

errorCases.scenario: Resume would overwrite uncommitted local changes to the files it restores
errorCases.detection: git status --porcelain on the files to restore is non-empty
errorCases.response: Return refused naming the files; nothing is touched
errorCases.userImpact: The new owner commits or stashes first

errorCases.scenario: Restoring the draft files fails part way (disk full, permission)
errorCases.detection: A write or rename in the restore loop throws or returns an error
errorCases.response: Remove every file this call already restored, restore any file it replaced from the pre-restore copy kept in memory, save no state, and return refused naming the failing file
errorCases.userImpact: The working tree is exactly as it was before the resume

errorCases.scenario: Resume cannot fetch the handoff branch
errorCases.detection: git ls-remote distinguishes a missing ref (empty result) from a failed command (ok:false)
errorCases.response: A missing branch falls back to restart on the committed artifacts; a network or permission failure is refused with the git message
errorCases.userImpact: A lost-machine takeover works without a branch; a network failure is not mistaken for a missing branch

errorCases.scenario: The upstream artifacts moved since the run was created
errorCases.detection: The run checkpoint's upstream snapshot of { artifactId, revision } (captured by snapshotUpstream when the run was created) is compared with readRevision of each file on the receiving clone, a missing revision reading as 0 on both sides
errorCases.response: Return refused 'the upstream moved since this run started' naming the artifacts, and offer the restart
errorCases.userImpact: The new owner redoes the stage on current input instead of resuming a stale one

errorCases.scenario: The workflow named for a resume does not match the unit or the artifact chain
errorCases.detection: resumeStage compares opts.workflow with authorUnitOf for the unit and with inferStageWorkflow
errorCases.response: Return refused naming the mismatch, for example a plan requested while the LLD is missing
errorCases.userImpact: The new owner is told which stage is actually next

edgeCases.input: The same unit is parked twice (the second owner is reassigned too)
edgeCases.expected: The deterministic branch name is reused and the new checkpoint is committed on top; a non-fast-forward push is reported as someone else having parked first

edgeCases.input: A run parked at stage awaiting_plan, before the decomposer plan was submitted
edgeCases.expected: The run checkpoint has no executor state; resume rebinds the intents and returns the emit_plan turn with a fresh token

edgeCases.input: A run parked at stage awaiting_synthesize

alternativesConsidered.name: Park-time checkpoint (run or draft-only) on a handoff branch, delivered through daemon-hosted park and resume
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Parking writes a run checkpoint or a draft-only checkpoint, with the draft artifacts, to a handoff branch, pushes it and notes it on the issue; resume validates the registration and repository identity, restores it on the new owner's daemon, rebound to that clone.
alternativesConsidered.approach: A handoff module under src/workflow/team owns two checkpoint variants written to .insrc/handoff/<unit-key>.json: a run checkpoint (the run's complete state at stage awaiting_plan, awaiting_llm_step or awaiting_synthesize, plus the owner, the upstream revisions captured when the run was created, and the repository identity) and a draft-only checkpoint (artifact files and identity, no run). The state store entry gains an owner and an upstream snapshot, set in handleStart through encodeState and carried through reencodeState and replaceState, and a listing function. Park commits through a temporary worktree so the user's checkout never changes, pushes, and adds one note through port.issueOps.comment. Resume takes the unit and, optionally, the workflow (inferred from the artifact chain when absent); it checks the repo is registered and is the checkpoint's repository, fetches the deterministic branch, validates the checkpoint, compares the stored upstream snapshot with current revisions, restores the files (rolling them back on failure), rebinds both intents, saves the run and returns the next turn (emit_plan, emit_step or emit_synthesize). With no branch, or a draft-only checkpoint, it returns restart (with the draft restored for draft-only). Park and resume are two new phases of insrc_workflow_step and two daemon RPC operations used by the terminal's team park and team resume.
pros: Meets ac25 to ac27, and ac28 at stage level, with one push at park time
Handles every stage a refused run can be in, including awaiting_plan
Reuses ExecutorState, runGit and issueOps.comment; no tracker abstraction change; park never touches the user's checkout
cons: Ownership and an upstream snapshot are captured on every run creation, and the codec and start handler change
Two checkpoint variants and a rollback path add test surface
Two new workflow-step phases and two daemon RPC operations

alternativesConsidered.name: Artifacts-only park, restart the stage on resume
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Parking commits whatever artifact files exist and notes the branch; resuming always restarts the stage from its first step with the parked draft as context.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Park commits the unit's draft artifact files to the handoff branch, pushes, and comments the branch on the issue. No run state is stored, so there is no ownership capture, snapshot, checkpoint schema or rebinding. Resume restores the files and starts the stage again from step one.
pros: Smallest change: no checkpoint schema and no state-store changes
One resume path for parked and lost-machine cases
cons: Fails ac27 for a stage parked before synthesize: none of the first developer's step outputs travel
Redoes completed model steps the first developer already paid for
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Smallest, but it violates ac27 for the common mid-run case, which is the point of the Story.

alternativesConsidered.name: Continuous checkpoint to a per-unit handoff branch
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Every completed step of a claimed unit commits and pushes its checkpoint, so a lost machine loses at most one step.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Extend a1 so each completed step writes the checkpoint and draft artifacts to the handoff branch through a managed second worktree, pushing in the background with a short deadline. Parking then only adds the note and a final push.
pros: Parking is cheap and cannot fail on a dirty working tree
cons: A commit and network push on every step of every team run, rejected by the user for its cost
Needs a managed worktree, background push failure reporting and branch rights for every developer
Changes the hot path of all four workflow-step phases
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Meets ac28 at step level, which the user decided is not needed (docs/plans/team-workflow.md, s6 decision on ac28), at the cost of a commit and push on every step of every team run.
